name: eclipticam-hq16
label: HQ16
label_notes: Peter's name for it (2026-10-13): HQ camera + 16 mm lens. It ran its first ~25 minutes on 10-13 as eclipticam-hq, writing to night/2026-10-13/hq/; those frames were moved into hq16/ at the rename.
camera: Raspberry Pi HQ Camera (IMX477) + 16 mm C-mount lens
cam_idx_notes: CSI port cam1 on the Pi 5, beside v3w (imx708_wide) on cam0. Pinned in /boot/firmware/config.txt with camera_auto_detect=0, dtoverlay=imx708,cam0 and dtoverlay=imx477,cam1,rotation=0 (hand-set 2026-10-13; ansible to own it).

lens.focus: manual; epoch 1 set by hand 2026-10-13, epoch 2 lens refitted 2026-10-25 (not refocused), epoch 3 focus search #1 on 80 m trees 2026-11-02, epoch 5 star-focused 2026-11-12

lens_notes: Manual 16 mm C-mount lens, fixed focus and iris: neither is under software control, so lens_position is null and the FITS carry no LENSPOS. Epoch 1 (10-13..10-25): no C-CS ring (none in the HQ box, though the datasheet says it ships with one), lens on a few threads of a wound-out back-focus ring. The YINETTECH 5-pack from Amazon (10-14) does not fit. Epoch 2 (10-25): the one genuine Raspberry Pi ring fitted. Focus 2026-10-13 was 'will have to do' at dusk, not a star-verified best; aperture setting not recorded.
brightness_baseline_notes: Epoch 3, focus search #1. Epoch 2 (10-25..11-02) was badly out of focus and ~3x brighter sky for an unexplained reason, so it does not join the baseline.
plate_scale_notes: SOLVED 2026-10-13 by astro-deliverables (astrometry.net on muppet, binned frame 1791927010433, ~22:30 BST): 39.8 arcsec per 2x2 binned pixel = 19.9 per photosite at full res (0.005528 deg); field 22.41 x 16.85 deg; centre RA 332.47 Dec -9.98 at that moment; up is -162.2 deg E of N. WCS at muppet ~/tmp/hqsolve/hqbin.wcs. Nominal was 19.98 (1.55 um / 16 mm). Epoch 1 only: refitting the lens with the C-CS adapter may shift it slightly.
position_index_notes: Calibration epoch, same convention as astrocam and eclipticam-v3w: INCREMENT whenever the camera, lens or mounting changes. Stamped as POSINDEX.

1.notes: First light. Lens without its C-CS adapter, held by a couple of threads on a back-focus ring wound out ~6 turns.

2.notes: Genuine Raspberry Pi C-CS adapter fitted ~15:30 GMT 10-25 (the only good ring in the house; the YINETTECH Amazon rings do not fit). Refocus and a new plate solve needed. Far out of focus throughout: no measurable stars (v3w saw 68 at 10-31 19 UTC, HQ16 none); see strand astro-hq16.

3.notes: Focus search #1 (Peter, ~15:00 GMT 11-02): camera re-aimed at daylight targets, lens focus ring at infinity and locked, aperture fully open (f/1.4, Peter's recollection), focus set on the back-focus ring by libcamera FocusFoM on trees ~80 m away (3.2 um inside infinity, under 1 binned px); aerial ~30 m and brick courses ~10 m also in view. Pointing changed: re-solve the plate and recheck the privacy margin. MEASURED (astro-hq16 disc.py, 11-02 02:00-02:45 UTC, 946 discs): blur D 14.8 binned px = 46 um, defocus 64 um PAST infinity (Peter overshot the tree focus), tilt ~28 um corner to corner (TL 62 TR 73 BL 45 BR 56). CAUTION: on 11-03 before dusk Peter turned the back-focus ring (angle not recorded) the wrong way, so frames from 11-03 dusk to ~18:38 UTC still carry POSINDEX 3 but sit at ~160 um (D ~37 px, 18:19-18:23 UTC).

4.notes: Focus search #2 (Peter, ~18:38 UTC 11-03, under cloud): back-focus ring turned back toward focus after the wrong-way turn; angle not recorded yet. Measure with astro-hq16 disc.py on the first clear frames. MEASURED (disc.py, 11-03 18:42-20:41 UTC, ~1500 discs): D 11.5-13.0 binned px, defocus 50-54 um past infinity, steady over 2 h; tilt pattern as epoch 3 (TL 54 TR 63 BL 41 BR 49).

5.notes: Focus search #3 (Peter, 11-12 dusk, live view 8 s gain 16 on stars): back-focus ring turned the same way as the 11-03 18:38 turn, about half as far; Peter: 'we have focus'. Angle not recorded. Pointing unchanged from epoch 4 (alt ~19.7 az ~203.7). TO MEASURE: FWHM/tilt map on the first clear frames (astro-hq16).

pedestal_notes: CHART FLOOR ONLY: the log2(mean/pedestal) axis reference, chosen for footroom below black_level, not a measurement. 200 on this 12-bit sensor is the same place as 50 on the 10-bit IMX708s (x4).
sky_mag_notes: astro-science 2026-10-31, PROVISIONAL +/-0.3: same-sky transfer from v3w on the one clean night (10-20, ratio 4.98), epoch 1, 60 s. Epoch 2 (from 10-25) is unconfirmed: recheck near new moon.
black_level_notes: IMX477 electronic zero in 12-bit LSB-aligned ADU (libcamera tuning 4096 at 16-bit). NOMINAL, not measured: cap the lens for a master dark.
detrans_notes: Measured 2026-11-13 (astro-hq16 #1083) on night 11-12 (epoch 5): star centroids matched between frames 10 min apart, 4 pairs 02-03 UTC, 7-22 matches each: (210.2, 79.9) binned px per 600 s, so 0.375 binned px/s = 1.849e-4 of the width per second, angle 20.8 deg (image x right, y down). The epoch-4 plate solve predicts 0.359 at 25.0 deg at the centre (22-29 deg across the field); the measurement wins. Pointing-dependent: re-measure after any move (a new position_index). crop is 0: no barrel to trim.
distortion_notes: 16 mm rectilinear lens over a 22 x 17 deg field: no measurable barrel (a plain TAN plate solve fits). Zero here so detrans-sweep does not apply its v3w default (k1 -0.636).
capture_notes: Night streaming params for eclipticam/hq16_night_daemon.py, which reads them (env HQ_EXPOSURE_US / HQ_GAIN override per host). 60 s matches v3w's cadence. buffer_count 2 rather than the house 4 because this 1 GB host also streams v3w at full res; the systemd unit caps the daemon's memory so an OOM takes this camera, not v3w. BUFFER: /mnt/ssd/eclipticam-buffer/hq16 on the local SSD, the first eclipticam stream off the 50M RAM tmpfs (2026-10-13, same night as first light). streaming.py refuses to run unless the buffer is on the /mnt/ssd mount, and the units carry RequiresMountsFor=/mnt/ssd.
rotate_180_notes: The camera IS mounted upside down, but the 180 degree turn is done by the driver (dtoverlay imx477 rotation=0 flips at the sensor), so every tool's output is already upright and libcamera reports RGGB. Do NOT also set a software rotation_180: that would turn the frames back over.
night_layout_notes: night/<night-date>/hq16/HH/<epoch_ms>.fits.fz beside v3w's night/<night-date>/v3w/, written by the shared v3w_uploader.py with V3W_SUBCAM=hq16.
processing_notes: Processed on muppet from bigstore (compute follows the data; eclipticam has ~137 MB free beside v3w). Public from 2026-10-15 (Peter asked for night cards on /astro/eclipticam/hq16); its field is sky only, above v3w's privacy crop (v3w rows 639-1010 vs keep-top 1064), so no privacy crop of its own. Re-check after the C-CS refit moves the pointing. No sky_clear_max_stops yet: a clear night sets it (falls back to 10.0).
night_output_notes: Products go in night/<night>/hq16/ beside the hour dirs, not night/<night>/ where v3w's live (astro/frames.py night_output_dir).
glow_sweep_notes: publish-night-cam builds the night's sky-glow model (skyglow-model cube + fit, in night/<n>/hq16/) and renders the glow sweep (diff-sweep --glow-model) behind derot-sky's clean gate, though HQ16 has no camera model for derot (astro-pipeline #1066, 2026-11-13, at Peter's ask via astro-hq16). Clean-gate noise reference: derot-sky CLEAN_NOISE_REF, from 2026-11-12.

field_solve.notes: Centre/size/orientation of the HQ16 field from astro-hq16's plate solve (epoch 4, unchanged pointing into epoch 5 per astro-hq16 #1083). Fixed in alt-az, so bin/derot-annotate carries it to any night. Replace with the epoch-5 solve (#455).
